Neiel
neh-EYE-el
proper noun
A town on the border of the tribe of Asher, named in the marking out of its bounds; the name is taken to mean “moved of God” or “dwelling of God.”

Biblical Definition

Neiel was a town on the border of Asher, named as the surveyor’s line turned toward the sunrising: the border “turneth toward the sunrising to Bethdagon, and reacheth to Zebulun, and to the valley of Jiphthahel toward the north side of Beth-emek, and Neiel” (Jos 19:27). It is a boundary-town, named nowhere else. The name is compounded with the name of God, and is taken by some to mean moved of God, and by others dwelling of God. If the former, it preaches the truth that God’s people are moved and led by Him: “For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God” (Rom 8:14). The believer does not order his own steps; the LORD directeth his going, moving him by His Spirit and His providence along the path of life. If the latter sense be preferred, dwelling of God, then the town speaks of the great mystery that God is pleased to dwell with men: He who inhabiteth eternity dwells also with the humble and contrite, and His people are His temple. Either way, the little border-town of Asher carries the name of God upon it, a witness that the people of God are known by His name, moved by His hand, and made the dwelling of His presence. To be moved of God and to be indwelt by God is the whole blessedness of the saint.

Webster 1828 Definition

A border town of Asher whose name means “moved of God” or “dwelling of God”; a witness that God’s people are led by His Spirit and made His dwelling.

NEIEL, a town on the border of Asher.

It is named in the tracing of that tribe’s bounds (Jos 19:27).

The name is compounded with the name of God.

It is taken to mean moved of God, or dwelling of God.

It witnesses that God’s people are led by His Spirit and indwelt by Him.

Key Scripture

Jos 19:27 — "And turneth toward the sunrising to Bethdagon, and reacheth to Zebulun, and to the valley of Jiphthahel toward the north side of Bethemek, and Neiel, and goeth out to Cabul on the left hand,"

Rom 8:14 — "For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God."

Isa 57:15 — "For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones."

1Co 3:16 — "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?"

Modern Corruption

A town of Scripture whose name bears the name of God; it recovers the truth that God’s people are moved by His Spirit and made the dwelling of His presence.

expand to see more

Neiel faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth its name carries answers the autonomous spirit that reckons a man the master of his own steps, owing his movements and his dwelling to none, and knowing nothing of being led or indwelt by God.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the leading and indwelling of God. A border-town bearing God’s name witnesses that His people are moved of God, led by His Spirit as sons, and made His dwelling, for He inhabiteth eternity yet dwells with the contrite. To be moved of God and indwelt by God is the whole blessedness of the saint.
